does: Cooks onions slowly until their water is gone and their sugars turn deep brown, soft and sweet.

intro.what: This onion method cooks sliced onions slowly until they become soft, sweet and deeply browned.
intro.why: It teaches patience with browning and how to respond when the pan colours faster than the onions.

how: Sweat sliced onions in butter with a little salt until soft.
Take the lid off and keep the heat at medium-low.
Stir every little while, scraping up the brown film that forms on the bottom of the pan.
Add a spoonful of water whenever the film darkens faster than the onions.
Stop when they are the colour of dark honey all the way through.

cues.text: An even, deep amber, a fraction of the raw heap, with no black edges.
Sweet and nutty, like toast and caramel. A sharp, acrid smell means they are burning.
As sweet as jam, with no sharpness left.

mistakes.mistake: Rushing with high heat, which burns the edges and leaves the middle pale and bitter.
mistakes.fix: Keep the heat low and give it the time it takes. There is no shortcut.

mistakes.mistake: Crowding a small pan, so that the onions steam and never brown.
mistakes.fix: Use the widest pan you have.

quiz.question: What is the aim of this onion method?
choices: Pale onions with a raw crunch.
Black edges around a pale centre.
quiz.because: Slow cooking lets onions become soft, sweet and deeply browned throughout.

quiz.question: After the onions have softened, how do you continue caramelizing them?
choices: Keep them covered over high heat.
Remove the lid and use medium-low heat.
Stop before they take any colour.
quiz.because: Remove the lid and continue over medium-low heat so the onions can brown gently.

quiz.question: Which colour are you aiming for when caramelizing these onions?
choices: Soft and glassy without any browning.
Even deep amber without black edges.
quiz.because: Aim for even deep amber. Black edges show that some of the onion has gone beyond browning.

quiz.question: The brown film in the pan darkens faster than the onions. What would you do?
choices: Add a little water and scrape up the film.
Raise the heat to catch the onions up.
Scrape only at the end so the brown film has time to develop.
quiz.because: A little water loosens the brown film before it darkens too far. Scrape it back into the onions.

comes_after.why: Onions sweat before they caramelize. The first stage is the same move.
